The M1 Macbook Air 2020 comes with a 1 year liquid/breakage warranty with a caller support from the apple itself. 
You can check the details by the help of your serial number in the backside of the macbook box case. By inputting your serial number in the site checkcoverage.apple.com you can check the warranty information and even you can check the product's genuinity.

Inorder to check the product's genuinity input your serial number and the captcha in the above mentioned site before before turning on your macbook(before opening your macbook air's lid). If the product is genuine, it will show 'Purchased date not updated' or sth like that.

Now inorder to check the warranty info you can input the same serial number after completely setting up your macbook air. 

I got mine with full year breakage warranty and the product was properly sealed with a fragile tag and the order track number.

The fridge was great as expected .

The overal impression is good, working well, looks alright.
There are two points not alright however.
We had the same but older Whirlpool model, which is now replaced by this new one. The issue is that in the previous model the vegetable drawer was not huge but good, but in this newer model it's significantly smaller. This makes no sense whatsoever, because the drawer from the old fridge does fit, so the space is there.
The second point is that there is a protective plastic foil on the plastic parts of both doors. This is meant to be removed, but after removal of this foil, it leaves large areas of glue behind. In a dusty city like KTM these glue stains will get black and dirty very quickly. One could choose to leave the foil but below the foil, there are air bubbles and white grit, which in my opinion looks hideous.
Conclusion, good fridge but the "opposite of an improvement" in the design and unprofessional finish.

(FYI, not a real refrigerator since it uses a fan to cool the contents, not a refrigerant). Otherwise product is good. It says it's compatible with 12V DC systems, such as those in cars, but you don't get extra cables and will have to use the 2 prong AC power cable, which is inefficient and draws up to 100W power instead of the stated 62W. I looked inside, and the power is fed into the chip via a AC 220 V module. The packaging mentions the inclusion of a power supply unit, but I'm not sure if it means the one already connected, or a spare 12V DC one (there was no such items in the box). Couldn't find any information online either. Also, the one I got came in a mouldy box and was made in 2017. (See pics).

If you're ok with figuring out how to solder on a 12V DC connection by yourself, or if 12V DC isn't a factor for you, then I recommend getting the product.

Cons:
